newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends on 11-week low on technical rout.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends on 11-week low on technical rout.

text.p: COMEX copper slumped to an eleven-week low on chart-based selling and the continued rise in LME stocks showed no sign of abating soon, dealers said.
Most-active September COMEX copper settled 4.50 cents weaker at 105.05 cents a lb, traded 110.10 to 104.80 cents. Spot July went out 4.15 cents lower at 107.40 cents.
"I think technically the market broke down, hit some sell stops which prompted some fund selling," Lawson Spence of broker Smith Barney said.
The market slipped through some key levels and stops were hit on LME and COMEX as the market wades through a seasonally slow period, Fred Demler of E D & F Man International said.
There was no fresh fundamental news to prompt the slide.
"Commodity funds across the board were initiating new sell order positions and covering long positions," Demler said.
There has been some producer selling in recent sessions, and LME inventory continues to rise, though this is offset to some degree by COMEX stock declines, Demler added.
Tuesday, LME stocks rose 2,250 tonnes to 133,350 tonnes, and COMEX stocks fell 1,547 short tons to 39,722 tons.

A strike at the Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal contnued Tuesday despite after a meeting between the workers and management failed to resolve a dispute which the market has so far largely ignored.
The key prop in the market, dealers said, was the continued strong cash to three months backwardation which ended Tuesday only slightly weaker at $128/$134.
